title: API Surface Harmonizer: OpenAI ChatCompletions request/response mapping
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a stable, auditable mapping layer that accepts OpenAI Chat Completions (v1/stream) style requests and produces Redwood-native internal events and vice-versa for responses. This harmonizer must preserve streaming semantics, function/tool calling boundaries, and structured output markers while adding Redwood routing metadata (model_variant, routing_hint) without breaking existing OpenAI-compatible clients.
background: We have many customers using OpenAI's chat completions API patterns. Our current proxies (various ad-hoc shims) introduce subtle behavioral differences: streaming chunks arrive reordered on tool-call boundaries, function_call objects are split across events unpredictably, and structured outputs lose annotations. This ticket consolidates a single, well-documented mapping implementation that is maintainable and testable across hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
design_notes: Key design decisions: 1) Introduce a canonical event model (line-delimited JSON events) inside the service that has explicit types: message.delta, message.finish, tool.call_start, tool.call_arg, tool.call_end, fallback_notice. 2) Mapping is two-way: inbound (OpenAI request -> internal route + normalized prompt envelope) and outbound (internal events -> OpenAI-style SSE stream). 3) Preserve idempotency and allow clients to set x-request-id which passes through. 4) For function/tool calling we will emit deterministic chunking rules: tool.call_start must appear in the same SSE event as the first tool.call_arg to match client hooks. 5) Provide a strict structured output validator that can inject advisories as separate events instead of mutating content. 6) Triage and document edge cases where behavior cannot be 1:1 due to Redwood features (e.g., routing fallbacks cause mid-stream model-switch notices).
acceptance_criteria: Roundtrip parity test: given a representative OpenAI chat request fixture the replayed stream from our harmonizer must be consumable by an unmodified OpenAI client lib without errors.

Tool/function calling: function_call objects must be emitted as a single logical call sequence in the SSE stream with a start, zero-or-more args, and end events; clients receive the same ordering as OpenAI's documented behavior.
Structured outputs: JSON schema anchors ("@@structured-output@@") preserved and represented as separate advisory events so downstream parsers can reconstruct typed outputs.
Backpressure and cancellation: when client disconnects we propagate a cancel event to the runtime and emit a final 'client.disconnect' audit event.
Observability: each stream contains trace_id and routing_hint headers; events are logged to audit store with raw payload for 30 days (configurable).
Non-regression: no existing SDK integration tests fail after toggle to harmonizer behind feature flag.
Performance: median end-to-end latency for lightweight prompts increases by <3ms at p50 in canary traffic (measure via runtime-1.22 canary).
tasks: Spec: finalize event model and document mapping matrix (OpenAI fields -> internal event types).
Implement inbound transformer (request shaping + header pass-through).
Implement outbound event streamer with deterministic chunking semantics.
Add structured-output validator and advisory-event emitter.
Integrate with audit logging pipeline and ensure retention + access policies.
Feature-flag rollout: implement toggle and canary routing in the console.
SDK: add compatibility tests for JS/Python to assert stream replay works.
Load tests: run 10k concurrent streams and observe CPU + latency profiles.
Security review and threat modeling for payload passthrough (PII/leakage).
